method: Headless Blender 5.1.1 (blender --background --python), MPFB 2.0.15 extension enabled via bpy.ops.preferences.addon_enable; GLB read-back via @gltf-transform/core NodeIO (the same instrument the planted contracts use).

bakeQuestion.question: Does the shipped MPFB2 enhanced_skin node tree (data/node_trees/enhanced_skin.json, loaded through MaterialService) bake to a baseColorTexture that survives glTF export under Blender 5.1 headless?
bakeQuestion.answer: NOT AUTOMATICALLY through the glTF exporter; YES via an explicit Cycles bake step. The exporter has NO material-bake capability in Blender 5.1; the shipped node tree's output survives export only when the pipeline bakes it to an image and wires that image into a Principled baseColor.

measurements.result: exported skin material has baseColorTexture=NONE, baseColorFactor=[1,1,1,1]. The enhanced_skin node tree's output does not survive export untouched.
measurements.evidence: NodeIO read-back of /tmp/bake_q_enhanced.glb: 'MAT: test_skin | baseColorTexture: NONE | factor: [1,1,1,1]'

measurements.experiment: Exporter capability: introspected bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf operator properties and searched io_scene_gltf2 source for material baking
measurements.result: No bake_materials/material-bake property exists in Blender 5.1's glTF exporter (only export_materials enum EXPORT/PLACEHOLDER/VIEWPORT/NONE, export_image_format etc.). The exporter never bakes procedural node graphs.
measurements.evidence: Full operator property list dumped via get_rna_type(); grep for 'bake' in addons_core/io_scene_gltf2 found only export_bake_animation (skeletal animation baking), not material baking.

measurements.experiment: Explicit Cycles bake: create_human -> create_v2_skin_material -> add ShaderNodeTexImage (active) -> render.engine=CYCLES CPU -> bpy.ops.object.bake(type='DIFFUSE', pass_filter={'COLOR'}, use_clear=True) -> wire baked image into a fresh Principled Base Color -> export
measurements.result: bpy.ops.object.bake succeeds (BAKE_OK, 1,042,362-byte PNG). The exported GLB carries baseColorTexture='probe_baked_skin' (1,042,362 B) on the skin material. The baked texture survives glTF export.
measurements.evidence: NodeIO read-back of /tmp/bake_q_full.glb: 'MAT: probe_exportable_skin | baseColorTexture: probe_baked_skin (1042362B) | factor: [1,1,1,1]'. Baked PNG has 67 distinct coarse colours (real variation, not a flat fill).

bakeQuestion.conclusion: The enhanced_skin route is VIABLE but only with an explicit Cycles bake step in the materializer. glTF carries no procedural shaders; a node graph alone reaches no learner. The slice must: (1) load the shipped node tree via MaterialService.create_v2_skin_material, (2) drive tone from phenotype (MpfbSkinMasterColor 'colorgroup' SkinColor input), (3) Cycles-bake the skin surface to a texture, (4) wire that texture into the exported Principled baseColor.
